scenario.name: Okta Security, Cloudflare & BeyondTrust — Support Case .har File sid Session Token Theft & Admin API Token Minting
scenario.shortSubtitle: Okta Security · Cloudflare SIRT · BeyondTrust · HTTP Archive (.har) Cookie: sid=... Replay · Post-MFA Admin Hijack
scenario.overview: Imagine a busy customer-support desk where enterprise administrators mail in full browser traffic recordings to help troubleshoot login glitches, forgetting to black out their own live master wristbands printed inside the packet headers. After breaching the support ticket vault, an intruder lifts those still-live master wristbands straight out of the uploaded recordings, replays them from an overseas proxy to walk straight past multi-factor locks, and mints permanent master API keys before alert response teams slam the door. In this scenario (T1539, Okta Security, Cloudflare & BeyondTrust, Support Case .har File sid Session Token Theft & Admin API Token Minting), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: harvesting Live Cookie: sid= Tokens, then replaying the sid Cookie from a Foreign VPN, then minting an Okta SSWS API Token. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Harvesting Live Cookie: sid= Tokens, then Replaying the sid Cookie from a Foreign VPN, then Minting an Okta SSWS API Token, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on Okta telemetry correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: EXTRACTING LIVE SID SESSION COOKIES FROM SUPPORT .HAR FILES
stages.subtitle: Parsing unsanitized Chrome DevTools HTTP Archive (.har) files for Cookie: sid=...
stages.description: Ransacking a compromised support-case filing cabinet, the intruder opens raw browser network recordings uploaded by helpful IT admins and immediately extracts active, unredacted administrator session wristbands still stamped inside the headers. Using a compromised Okta support service account, the threat actor downloads HTTP Archive (.har) files attached to customer support tickets and parses the JSON entries[].request.cookies array to extract Cookie: sid=102f8a9c7e4b... (the primary bearer session cookie issued by Okta after the Super Administrator has already completed password and FIDO2/Okta Verify Multi-Factor Authentication). A .har file is not just a screenshot or timing chart; by specification, it is a full JSON archive of every HTTP request and response header, cookie, and POST body transmitted by the browser tab during recording. In the documented HAR JSON PARSE exchange from Support Case Threat Actor to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with RESP SID Token Live (confirming that the HAR_SID_COOKIE_EXTRACTED request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 REPLAYING SID COOKIE TO BYPASS MFA IN OKTA ADMIN CONSOLE). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ HAR_SID_COOKIE_EXTRACTED / ⇠#1 RESP SID Token Live) from Node ① (#1 Support Case Threat Actor) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Okta System Log & SIRT SIEM).

keySpecs.value: Browser HTTP Archive (.har) Uploaded to Support Portal

stages.title: REPLAYING SID COOKIE TO BYPASS MFA IN OKTA ADMIN CONSOLE
stages.subtitle: Impersonating the Super Administrator session from a foreign VPN IP (T1550.004)
stages.description: Pasting the lifted session wristband straight into their own browser from an overseas VPN booth, the intruder walks straight into the victim Super Admin control panel without ever typing a password or touching a hardware security key. Within 30 minutes of the .har file upload, the attacker sends an HTTPS GET request from a commercial VPN exit node (198.51.100.205, ASN 9009) to https://corp-admin.okta.com/admin/dashboard carrying Cookie: sid=102f8a9c7e4b... (hijacking the existing authenticated session trs102f8a9c7e4b without triggering any password check or MFA push notification, which Okta logs as user.session.access_admin_app under the exact same authenticationContext.externalSessionId). Why did BeyondTrust’s identity policy block the attacker at the console while other tenants allowed access? Because enforcing Admin Session IP Binding or device-bound Okta FastPass policies causes Okta to reject a valid sid cookie the moment the client IP or device posture changes. In the documented OKTA user.session.access_admin_app exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to Uploaded Browser .har Capture, Uploaded Browser .har Capture responds with ALERT MFA Bypassed via sid (confirming that the SESSION_ASN_ROAMING_DETECTED request succeeded on Uploaded Browser .har Capture and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 MINTING PERSISTENT SSWS API TOKENS & SIRT SESSION REVOCATION). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ SESSION_ASN_ROAMING_DETECTED / ⇠#2 ALERT MFA Bypassed via sid) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Uploaded Browser .har Capture), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Okta System Log & SIRT SIEM).

stages.title: MINTING PERSISTENT SSWS API TOKENS & SIRT SESSION REVOCATION
stages.subtitle: Creating an Okta SSWS API token before SIRT detects ASN roaming and kills the session
stages.description: Racing against the clock before the temporary wristband expires or defenders spot the sudden address jump, the intruder attempts to print permanent master API keys or bolt on a rogue identity bridge, triggering real-time security alarms at vigilant defender centers. Because the stolen sid cookie is tied to the victim admin’s browser session lifetime, the attacker immediately navigates to Security -> API -> Tokens in the Okta Admin Console to invoke system.api_token.create (minting a static SSWS bearer token named "BackupSyncToken" and creating a secondary Super Admin user, which Cloudflare SIRT detected in real time via SIEM alerts on session ASN roaming and neutralized by calling DELETE /api/v1/users/{id}/sessions and revoking all newly created API tokens). Following this incident, Cloudflare released an open-source client-side HAR Sanitizer (har-sanitizer.pages.dev) that automatically strips Cookie, Set-Cookie, and Authorization values before engineers share .har files. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ SSWS_API_TOKEN_CREATED / ⇠#3 ALERT TOKEN_REVOKED_BY_SIRT) from Node ③ (#3 Uploaded Browser .har Capture) to Node ④ (#4 Customer Okta Admin Console), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Okta System Log & SIRT SIEM).

detectionRule.title: Okta externalSessionId Roaming Across Multiple ASNs or Operating Systems
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Okta Session Cookie Replay Across Distinct ASNs
logsource:
  product: okta
  service: okta
detection:
  selection:
    eventType: 'user.session.access_admin_app'
  condition: selection | count(securityContext.asNumber) by authenticationContext.externalSessionId > 1
detectionRule.mitigation: Enable Okta Admin Console Session IP Binding and Continuous Access Evaluation to reject mid-session ASN changes.

detectionRule.title: Okta SSWS API Token Created or Super Admin Granted From Untrusted IP
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Okta API Token Created in Admin Console
logsource:
  product: okta
  service: okta
detection:
  selection:
    eventType:
      - 'system.api_token.create'
      - 'user.account.privilege.grant'
      - 'system.idp.lifecycle.create'
  condition: selection
detectionRule.mitigation: Require phishing-resistant FIDO2 re-authentication on every privileged Admin Console action and restrict API token creation to trusted corporate IP zones.
